paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: This plot, titled "Errors (COPA)," illustrates the generalization errors on the COPA dataset as a function of adapter rank. The x-axis is labeled "Rank" and uses a logarithmic scale with tick labels at 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis represents the error values on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to approximately 0.7, with tick marks at 0.0, 0.3, and 0.6. A single dark line with green circular markers connects the four data points, and each marker includes vertical error bars indicating variability. At rank 4, the error is approximately 0.16. The value decreases slightly to approximately 0.13 at rank 16. The error then increases notably to approximately 0.38 at rank 64. At rank 256, the error remains at a similar level of approximately 0.40. The error bars appear relatively small at ranks 4 and 16 and somewhat larger at ranks 64 and 256.
